title: The work list
dek: What is being done here, as opposed to what is known.
lead: Every other register in this archive answers what is **known** — [what has been searched](/searched/), [what is still open](/open-questions/), [what was got wrong](/corrections/). None of them answered **what is being done**, so that lived in a chat window, which is the one place that does not survive the session. Three times in one week someone asked this archive what it was working on, and three times the answer was typed out and then lost. This is that answer, written down. It is deliberately short on findings and long on **who has to move each thing** — an item with no owner is how a list becomes wallpaper.
close: Written 15 September 2026, in the shape the Defranceschi session settled on, so that eight archives keep one list rather than eight people each inventing one.

rows.what: Rebuild the Žubrinić households of Šumećica by house number, from the Otočac baptisms of 1846–58
rows.note: The thing [question 4](/open-questions/) now turns on. That book writes the household into its *Conditio* column — **«Confiniarius ex Poljica 14»**, **«e Šumećica N° 2»** — so the column can be harvested. **Three houses are established so far: N° 2 (Nicolaus, 1856 and 1858), N° 10 (Michael × Helena Orešković of Prozor, 1846), N° 24 (Michaël × Maria Orešković, 1834).** Seven indexed Michael entries between 1847 and 1858 are still unread. **The obstacle is measured:** the record index gives the ARK of the **opening**, not the row, so each entry costs two or three crops to find.

rows.what: Read Karlobag marriage folios 6 and 4 entry by entry, for ahnentafel 54's marriage
rows.note: Folios 2 to 6 — 1804 to early 1810, the whole window a daughter born 23 April 1810 allows — are read and hold **no Uroda × Gerkacs**. Folio 8 is eliminated: it is 1811–12, too late. What remains is a slower second pass looking for *Uroda* and *Gerkacs* **inside** each entry rather than at its head. **Expect a negative**, and record it as one.

rows.what: Selce deaths 1816–1886 — six direct ancestors, none read
rows.note: Ahnentafel 24, 25, 48, 49, 50 and 51 all die in that span. **DGS 5497948.** The record index reaches Selce *baptisms* only, so this one is a film read. It is the largest untouched block of direct-line evidence left.

rows.what: Senj marriages 1734–1858 — the marriage of ahnentafel 12 and 13
rows.note: Their son was baptised **1 November 1857**, so the marriage falls just before it. Their register names are now known exactly — **«Juraj Papa, težak»** and **«Matia rođena Pilipić»** — which is what makes this findable. Not in the index; a film read.

rows.what: Ahnentafel 53's baptism — Oliva Maria Smojver, Karlobag, March 1781
rows.note: A lead rather than a finding: the index holds **«Smoj[v]er, 23 February 1782, father Vincentio, mother Oliva»** — a Karlobag household with a mother called **Oliva** the year after ahnentafel 53 was born. Her own baptism is **not indexed** (four Karlobag Smojver entries before 1796 against 114 after), so this is a page to open on that opening, not a join to make.

rows.what: Four books located this week and never opened
rows.note: **Bribir** 1678 onward — its own parish, filed here as a village of Grižane until the catalogue was read properly. **Sv. Juraj kod Senja** 1697–1852, not in the parish table at all. The **Karlobag *Stanje duša*** beyond the U section. The **Grižane *Popis duša* of 1738**, a household census a century older than Otočac's. All four are in [holdings.psv](/searched/) with their film numbers.

rows.what: The one village in the Otočac census whose name could not be read
rows.note: Image 75. Every other *Pagus* in the book was mapped — Ottosaz, Luka, Dubrava, Novoselia, Lieška, Kostelievo Selo, Obilje, Beljue, Šumećica — and this one resisted. Small, but the map is otherwise complete and a hole in it will be noticed.

rows.what: Reconcile the stale «pending» rows in the searched register
rows.note:
**Done 15 September 2026.** Three rows were retired, not edited: **Ancestry**, **FamilySearch — Rijeka registers** and **FamilySearch — Otočac, Stanje duša** were *placeholders* — «never», «not yet», «still unread» — and each had been superseded by a real row recording the actual reading. The register was **over-reporting what is outstanding**: eleven pending, of which three were already done. Seven now, and every one of them genuinely open.

**The gate that stops it recurring.** Every register row now declares a `key` — the body of material it covers — and `tools/searched.py` **refuses** when a row is *pending* while any other row with the same key carries a real outcome. The key is there because the source *name* cannot do this job: «Senj marriages, 1734–1858» is genuinely unopened while «Senj marriages, 1859–1920» is read end to end, and a gate matching on names would have called the first one stale and sent a sitting to re-read a book that was already finished. A gate that cries wolf is worse than no gate.

The same stale claim had spread into prose: `/searched` still named **four portals «never once searched»** when all four had been opened, and `requests/README.md` and `REPLIES.md` still said the three letters were **not yet sent** when they went on the 15th. All corrected.

rows.what: Decide where ahnentafel 108 and 109 live
rows.note: **Georgius Uroda** and his wife **Maria** were read out of a register this week and are real. The tree stops at ahnentafel 54 and this archive does not edit the tree — that separation is what the whole project rests on. They are recorded in `sources/found.psv` with ten others, but **nothing on the site shows them** yet. Whether a found person should appear beside the tree, and how, is a decision about what this archive *is*, not a task.

rows.what: Waiting on the Državni arhiv u Rijeci
rows.note: Sent 15 September to **obrada@riarhiv.hr**. It asks for one identified volume: the Rijeka baptismal register covering **1 March 1892**, which the film skips — the volumes run 1886–90, 1890–91, then **1900–01**, and the alphabetical *Kazalo* skips the same span. **This is the only route left to [question 13](/open-questions/)**, and to Juraj's marriage with it.

rows.what: Waiting on the Župni ured Senj
rows.note: Sent 15 September to the parish priest. Three deaths after the film stops in 1907 — including **Milka Papić**, whose 1886 baptismal entry carries a registrar's 1971 annotation citing **page 280, line 37** — the January and February 1895 baptisms, and whether a *stanje duša* survives for Senj.

rows.what: Waiting on Župa Krmpote, via Ledenice
rows.note: Sent 15 September. Asks for **Juraj Blažević's baptism**, most likely 1855–70 and before the film begins — the single entry that would name his father and settle the join five generations rest on. **One question in that letter has since been answered here**: Tonka's date is **25/27 October 1884**, read off the register, and the reply should be read against that rather than the other way round.

rows.what: Waiting on the Državni arhiv u Gospiću
rows.note: Sent 13 September, **acknowledged and queued on the 14th**, nothing since. Gospić holds Otočac and Karlobag — which is to say the Žubrinići and the Urode.

rows.what: Arolsen Archives — needs a browser this machine cannot provide
rows.note: `collections.arolsen-archives.org` refuses this machine. It is the likeliest route to anything on **Senj, 1943**, and it has never been searched. Ten minutes in an ordinary browser.

rows.what: The alphabet nodes are probably not only a Žubrinić problem
rows.note: Fifteen nodes named with a single capital letter — **«M Žubrinić Xubrinich Zubrinic»** — were being published as parents of 75 real people and as one another's siblings. A card index typed in as a family. Both the bucket detector and the site's junk filter now refuse them, **but all seven archives share one GEDCOM**, and nothing here has checked whether the same drawers exist under Blažević, Papić, Prpić or Kalanj. **The test is four lines** and belongs in the kit rather than in this archive.

rows.what: Three methods found here that the other archives will need
rows.note: **The index gives the image.** FamilySearch's record search returns the **image ARK** of every indexed entry, so a record opens at the page in one step instead of being hunted down a film — that single fact produced most of this week's findings. **A third FamilySearch failure state**: a sign-out takes *everything* (503, redirect to the sign-in host) where a rate-limit blip and a session block leave the catalogue answering — written into `tools/familysearch.md`. **And `sources/found.psv`**, somewhere to put people read out of a register whom the tree does not have; every archive here will hit that wall.

rows.what: Another session's kit upgrade is sitting half-landed in this working tree
rows.note:
**The styles.css instance cleared** — whoever wrote the burger-menu fix has committed or discarded it, and it is gone from the tree. A second instance took its place the same day.

`site/package.json` and `site/package-lock.json` now pin the kit at **`f55559d`** where the last commit here pinned **`60aad58`**, and `node_modules/` holds the newer one. Nothing in this archive's build script installs anything, so the bump was made by **the kit session running `npm install` in this shared tree**. It is real work — `f55559d` gives `WorkList.astro` the ring that links each archive's work list to the others — and the kit has already moved **one commit past it** (`27cfb83`), so the bump is mid-flight rather than finished.

**Left uncommitted deliberately.** This archive's build passes against the newer kit (check:kit, check:living and check:worklist all green), so nothing is broken; but committing another session's half-landed upgrade would take the decision of *which* kit commit the estate stands on away from the session making it. Every `git add` here stays scoped to `sources/ tools/ site/src/ notes/ requests/`.

rows.what: Read the Otočac status animarum to find the Žubrinići
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake and kept here rather than deleted.** Two sittings went into this book on the assumption it held the family. It does not: Šumećica occupies images 102–106, and every household in them is **Dašović, Štabinčić, Orehović, Janežić, Ollar, Kovačić or Orehovački** — no Žubrinić, no Domus 2, no Domus 24. The book gave the village map and a clean negative, and it will not give the house. **The baptism registers replaced it** — that is row 1.

rows.what: Find Juraj Blažević's baptism in the Krmpote film
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake.** The plan named this «the reachable target» on the strength of a catalogued range of *1815–1896*. The film begins in **1879** and Juraj was born in the 1860s; Krmpote is one film, one item, and there is no other Krmpote book. Ledenice and Novi Vinodolski were checked the same way and hold no candidate. **What survives is the letter** — row 12.

rows.what: Harvest house numbers from the Otočac baptisms of 1834–46
rows.note: **Founded on a mistake, and it was this archive's own.** The morning's plan said *every* entry writes the household into the *Conditio* column. **That book does not**: its *Conditio* holds one status word — *Confiniarius*, *Decurio* — checked at December 1839 and March 1845, with the place column giving only «Ottoccii». Ahnentafel 10's January 1834 entry is an early-book habit the parish dropped. **House numbers are readable for 1846–58 and for the first years of 1834, and not in between.**
